labels.primary: row 4, with one cell left

frames.text: Row 4 has one empty cell, r4c9, and lacks only 8.

step.description: Full House: r4c9 is the last empty cell in row 4, so it must be 8.

labels.primary: the cell with one candidate left
labels.secondary: the other eight digits, each already in its row, column or box

frames.text: Only one candidate is left in r4c1: 1.
The row, column and box of r4c1 already hold the other eight digits.

step.description: Naked Single: the row, column and box of r4c1 already hold the other eight digits, so r4c1 must be 1.

labels.primary: row 2: 1 has one place left in it
labels.secondary: the 1s that rule out its other cells, shaded along their lines

frames.text: In row 2, the 1 can go only in r2c2.
The 1s in r4c1, r1c5 and r7c9 rule out 1 in every other empty cell of row 2.

step.description: Hidden Single: 1 fits only in r2c2 within row 2.

labels.primary: box 4: every 3 in it sits on one row

frames.text: In box 4, the only cells that can take 3 are r5c1 and r5c3.
One of them must be 3, and both lie in row 5, so no other cell of row 5 can be 3.

step.description: Locked Candidates (Pointing): in box 4, every 3 lies in row 5, so no other cell of row 5 can be 3.

labels.primary: row 1: every 5 in it sits in one box

frames.text: In row 1, the only cells that can take 5 are r1c5 and r1c6.
One of them must be 5, and both lie in box 2, so no other cell of box 2 can be 5.

step.description: Locked Candidates (Claiming): in row 1, every 5 lies in box 2, so no other cell of box 2 can be 5.

labels.primary: two cells that hold only 2 and 5 between them, in row 9

frames.text: In row 9, r9c2 and r9c7 hold only 2 and 5.

walk.lead: They must be 2 and 5, one each: these digits can go nowhere else in row 9.

step.description: Naked Pair: in row 9, r9c2 and r9c7 hold only 2 and 5, so these digits can go nowhere else in row 9.

labels.primary: the only two cells of row 4 where 6 and 8 can go

frames.text: In row 4, the digits 6 and 8 can go only in r4c3 and r4c7.

walk.lead: They must be 6 and 8, one each, and hold nothing else: r4c3 and r4c7 keep only 6 and 8.

step.description: Hidden Pair: in row 4, the digits 6 and 8 can go only in r4c3 and r4c7, so these cells can hold nothing else.

labels.primary: three cells that hold only 2, 6 and 7 between them, in box 8

frames.text: In box 8, r7c4, r8c6 and r9c4 hold only 2, 6 and 7 between them.

walk.lead: They must be 2, 6 and 7, one each: these digits can go nowhere else in box 8.

step.description: Naked Triple: in box 8, r7c4, r8c6 and r9c4 hold only 2, 6 and 7 between them, so these digits can go nowhere else in box 8.

labels.primary: the only three cells of row 8 where 3, 5 and 9 can go

frames.text: In row 8, the digits 3, 5 and 9 can go only in r8c4, r8c6 and r8c9.

walk.lead: They must be 3, 5 and 9, one each, and hold nothing else: r8c4 keeps only 3 and 5; r8c6 keeps only 3 and 9.

step.description: Hidden Triple: in row 8, the digits 3, 5 and 9 can go only in r8c4, r8c6 and r8c9, so these cells can hold nothing else.

labels.primary: four cells that hold only 5, 6, 8 and 9 between them, in row 5

frames.text: In row 5, r5c4, r5c5, r5c6 and r5c9 hold only 5, 6, 8 and 9 between them.

walk.lead: They must be 5, 6, 8 and 9, one each: these digits can go nowhere else in row 5.

step.description: Naked Quadruple: in row 5, r5c4, r5c5, r5c6 and r5c9 hold only 5, 6, 8 and 9 between them, so these digits can go nowhere else in row 5.

labels.primary: base rows: the 7s of the fish
labels.secondary: cover columns: 2 of them take the base's 7s, so 7 goes nowhere else in them

frames.text: In rows 3 and 8, the 7s lie only in r3c3, r3c8, r8c3 and r8c8.
These cells lie in columns 3 and 8. Each of rows 3 and 8 needs a 7, and no column holds two, so each of columns 3 and 8 gets its 7 from one of rows 3 and 8.

walk.lead: No other cell of columns 3 and 8 can be 7.

step.description: X-Wing on 7: in rows 3 and 8, the 7s lie only in columns 3 and 8 (r3c3, r3c8, r8c3, r8c8). Those 2 rows will use up 7 in those 2 columns, so 7 can go nowhere else in them.

labels.primary: the only four cells of box 5 where 1, 2, 5 and 8 can go

frames.text: In box 5, the digits 1, 2, 5 and 8 can go only in r4c5, r4c6, r5c5 and r5c6.

walk.lead: They must be 1, 2, 5 and 8, one each, and hold nothing else: r4c5 keeps only 1 and 2; r4c6 keeps only 1 and 5; r5c5 keeps only 2 and 8.

step.description: Hidden Quadruple: in box 5, the digits 1, 2, 5 and 8 can go only in r4c5, r4c6, r5c5 and r5c6, so these cells can hold nothing else.

labels.primary: base columns: the 9s of the fish
labels.secondary: cover rows: 3 of them take the base's 9s, so 9 goes nowhere else in them

frames.text: In columns 1, 4 and 8, the 9s lie only in r3c1, r5c1, r4c4, r5c4, r3c8 and r4c8.
These cells lie in rows 3, 4 and 5. Each of columns 1, 4 and 8 needs a 9, and no row holds two, so each of rows 3, 4 and 5 gets its 9 from one of columns 1, 4 and 8.

walk.lead: No other cell of rows 3, 4 and 5 can be 9.

step.description: Swordfish on 9: in columns 1, 4 and 8, the 9s lie only in rows 3, 4 and 5 (r3c1, r5c1, r4c4, r5c4, r3c8, r4c8). Those 3 columns will use up 9 in those 3 rows, so 9 can go nowhere else in them.

labels.primary: base rows: the 6s of the fish
labels.secondary: cover columns: 4 of them take the base's 6s, so 6 goes nowhere else in them

frames.text: In rows 2, 6, 8 and 9, the 6s lie only in r2c5, r2c9, r6c5, r6c8, r8c6, r8c9, r9c6 and r9c8.
These cells lie in columns 5, 6, 8 and 9. Each of rows 2, 6, 8 and 9 needs a 6, and no column holds two, so each of columns 5, 6, 8 and 9 gets its 6 from one of rows 2, 6, 8 and 9.

walk.lead: No other cell of columns 5, 6, 8 and 9 can be 6.

step.description: Jellyfish on 6: in rows 2, 6, 8 and 9, the 6s lie only in columns 5, 6, 8 and 9 (r2c5, r2c9, r6c5, r6c8, r8c6, r8c9, r9c6, r9c8). Those 4 rows will use up 6 in those 4 columns, so 6 can go nowhere else in them.

labels.primary: box 1: its 5s all lie in row 1 or column 2
labels.secondary: r1c5 and r6c5: the only 5s in column 5

frames.text: In box 1, every 5 lies in row 1 or column 2: r1c2 and r1c3 in row 1, r2c2 in column 2.
r1c5 and r6c5 are the only 5s in column 5, so one of them is 5.

walk.lead: If r6c5 is 5, r6c2 sees it in row 6. If r1c5 is 5, row 1 has no other 5, so the 5 of box 1 must be in r2c2, which r6c2 sees in column 2. Either way r6c2 sees a 5.

step.description: The only 5s in column 5 are r1c5 and r6c5. If r6c5 is 5, r6c2 sees it in row 6. If r1c5 is 5, box 1 has no 5 left in row 1, so its 5 lies in column 2, which r6c2 sees too. So 5 is removed from r6c2.

links.text: The cells r2c3, r2c5, r3c4, r5c5 and r6c4 hold only 3 and 5. Each line joins two of them that see each other: they cannot hold the same digit, so their 3s take opposite shades, and so do their 5s.
If dark purple is true, the 3 in r2c3 is true, and the 3 in r6c3 goes.
If light purple is true, the 3 in r6c4 is true, and the 3 in r6c3 goes. Either way it is false.

step.description: Remote Pair: the cells r2c3, r2c5, r3c4, r5c5 and r6c4 hold only 3 and 5. Two of them that see each other cannot hold the same digit, so their 3s take opposite shades of purple, and so do their 5s: either every dark purple candidate is true, or every light purple one is. The 3 in r6c3 sees a dark purple 3 in r2c3 and a light purple 3 in r6c4, so it is false either way.

labels.primary: cells holding 4 and 6

step.description: W-Wing: r3c7 and r9c5 both hold 4/6; the strong link on 4 (r8c5–r8c7) forces one of them to be 6, removing 6 from cells seeing both.

labels.primary: the pivot and the digit each pincer shares with it

frames.text: The pivot r7c7 holds only 7 and 9.

labels.primary: the pivot

frames.text: If r7c7 is 7, the pincer r7c6 (only 6 and 7) must be 6.

labels.primary: the pivot and the digit the pincer shares with it

frames.text: If r7c7 is 9, the pincer r8c9 (only 6 and 9) must be 6.

walk.lead: Either way a pincer is 6; r7c8 and r8c6 see both.

step.description: XY-Wing: pivot r7c7 (7/9) with pincers r7c6 (6/7) and r8c9 (6/9); one pincer must be 6, so 6 is removed from cells seeing both.

labels.primary: the pivot's 5 and 9, and the one each pincer shares with it

frames.text: The pivot r2c5 holds only 4, 5 and 9.

labels.primary: the pivot's 5 and 9

frames.text: If r2c5 is 5, the pincer r3c6 (only 4 and 5) must be 4.

labels.primary: the pivot's 5 and 9, and the one the pincer shares with it
labels.secondary: 4 in the pivot and the pincer

frames.text: If r2c5 is 9, the pincer r7c5 (only 4 and 9) must be 4.

walk.lead: Or the pivot is 4 itself. Whichever digit it takes, one of the three cells is 4; r3c5 sees all three.

step.description: XYZ-Wing: pivot r2c5 (4/5/9) with pincers r3c6 (4/5) and r7c5 (4/9). Whichever digit the pivot takes, one of the three cells is 4, so 4 is removed from every cell that sees all three.
